en: The Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Banner of the Seal of the Wondrous Arm, translated by the Tripitaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan during the Great Tang Dynasty by Imperial Command.
Thus have I heard. At one time the Buddha was staying on Mount Kailāsa, the abode of various beasts, in the wondrous...
Within the palace,
he was together with a great assembly of twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus,
as well as with immeasurable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Mañjuśrī, the Prince of the Dharma, was the leader; all of them were in the form of youths,
together with the sixteen great men, such as Bhadrapāla and others.
At that time, the World-Honored One, with right mindfulness and wisdom,
expounded the essentials of the Dharma for the sake of the devas and humans,

causing them all to rejoice. Then the Great Brahmā King, along with the various devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others, [gathered there].
Each of them rose, joined their palms, and addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One, there are sentient beings who,
because they have committed various kinds of sinful and evil karma..."
They ought to fall into the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, and animals,
where they would undergo all manner of sufferings within the domain of Yama.
We only pray that the World-Honored One, out of great compassion, [will save us].
He taught the skillful means for eliminating such suffering and affliction,
so that those sentient beings might all attain liberation from the hardships of the evil realms.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
Furthermore, surrounded before and behind by immeasurable great ṛṣis who maintain mantras,
he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and said: “World-Honored One,
please deign to look upon us with compassion and save all the worlds through skillful means.”
The Buddha said, "Good son,
there is a dhāraṇī named 'Wondrous Arm-Seal Banner.
If one can constantly recite, practice, and contemplate it, [one shall attain liberation]."
One shall swiftly eliminate the five sins of immediate retribution and be born into a wealthy, noble, and secure family.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this incantation:
Tadyathā: kara kara, kiri kiri, kuru kuru, sara sara, ciri ciri, suru suru, sarvabuddhāvalokite, dhara dhara, dharmāvalokite, jvara jvara, saṃghāṭiśikhite, vara vara, varākani, buddhakoti-vaśite.
1. Kara kara 2. Kiri kiri 3. Kuru kuru 4. Sara sara 5. Ciri ciri 6. Suru suru 7. Sarvabuddhāvalokite 8.
Dhara dhara 9. Dharmāvalokite 10. Jvara jvara 11. Saṃghāṭiśikhite 12. Varā-varākani 13. Buddhakoti-vaśite
KṢAṆA KṢAṆA (14) SARVA-APARĀN-ME (15) SARVA-DUKHA-APANAYE (16) BRAHMA-BRAHMA (17) TARA-TARA (18) ṬAṬA ṬAṬA (19) SAPTAJA SAPTAJA (20) SARVA-APARĀN-APAYE (21) TUKKATE (22) Ni.
*Svāhā*. Twenty-three. Good son, this dhāraṇī has been spoken by Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Ānanda, a Buddha-world is difficult to encounter, and a human body is difficult to obtain.
To receive and uphold this mantra is even more difficult.
Son of good family, I recall the past,
from Vipaśyin Buddha down through the successive Buddhas until Kāśyapa Tathāgata.
Please expound this dhāraṇī for me,
for the sake of bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings;
it has been personally heard and received from all the Buddhas.
At that time, when the World-Honored One had spoken this mantra,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara and the rest,
along with the assembly of all eight classes of beings, including devas and nāgas, were present.
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken, they were all greatly rejoiced, and they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
*The Sūtra of the Dharani of the Banner of the Wondrous-Armed Seal*.
